questions.text: When performing gradient accumulation in PyTorch, which of the following statements are true?
options: Gradients computed by loss.backward() are added to the existing .grad attributes of model parameters rather than replacing them.
To accumulate gradients over multiple mini-batches before an optimizer step, you must call optimizer.zero_grad() after every loss.backward() .
Calling loss.backward() automatically clears the previously stored gradients in the model parameters.
Gradient accumulation in PyTorch is enabled by setting requires_grad=True for model parameters.
questions.correct_answer: Gradients computed by loss.backward() are added to the existing .grad attributes of model parameters rather than replacing them.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding Data Augmentation are correct?
options: Involves creation of modified copies of existing data through techniques such as rotation, scaling, cropping among others.
It artificially expands the dataset to help the model generalize better on unseen data and reduce overfitting.
The primary objective is to make the images smaller to achieve faster training.
It is used for the removal of noise from images and converting it to grayscale.
correct_answer: Involves creation of modified copies of existing data through techniques such as rotation, scaling, cropping among others.
It artificially expands the dataset to help the model generalize better on unseen data and reduce overfitting.

questions.text: What is the main difference between PIL.Image.open() and cv2.imread() when loading a color image?
options: Pillow loads the image as a NumPy array, while OpenCV loads it in a custom format.
Pillow (PIL) loads the image in RGB format, while OpenCV (cv2) loads it in BGR format.
questions.correct_answer: Pillow (PIL) loads the image in RGB format, while OpenCV (cv2) loads it in BGR format.
